cohort: The study included 120 discarded placentae, 60 from normal birth weight (> 2500gms) and 60 from low-birth-weight (<2500gms) full-term deliveries, collected at random from a medical college in India.
finding: The study found statistically significant differences in placental morphometric parameters (weight, volume, diameter, thickness, feto-placental ratio, and placental coefficient) between normal birth weight and low birth weight groups, indicating an association between placental morphometry and fetal weight.
cross-section timing: Data was collected at the time of delivery.
